title: Sensex Put Options Spike 500% as Closing Auction Triggers Another 2,100-Point Swing
excerpt: India's new closing auction session caused the Sensex to briefly plunge 2,100 points on expiry day, sending put option premiums surging and reigniting calls for SEBI to intervene.
body:
• Sensex put option premiums spiked 400-500% during Thursday's closing auction session as the index briefly dropped 2,100 points
  • The 30-stock index recovered to close just 0.55% lower at 76,152.86, while Nifty 50 ended 0.17% down
  • Thin BSE liquidity continues to amplify CAS swings on expiry days, with traders and analysts calling for SEBI to pause or redesign the mechanism
  • Cash market volumes on NSE fell to a five-month low in August as CAS uncertainty rattled investor confidence

Put option premiums on the BSE Sensex surged between 400% and 500% during Thursday's closing auction session as India's benchmark index briefly plunged over 2,100 points within minutes before snapping back, according to Reuters. The wild swing marked the third consecutive expiry-day disruption since the new auction mechanism launched on August 3.

The premium on the 76,400-point Sensex put option jumped to 247.05 rupees from 47.35 rupees during the auction window, BSE data showed. The Sensex's indicative close briefly slipped to around 74,370 from 76,510 before settling 417 points lower at 76,152.86 — a 0.55% decline. The Nifty 50 closed 0.17% lower at 23,873.45.

What Is the Closing Auction Session

SEBI introduced the closing auction session on August 3 to determine official closing prices for 208 F&O-eligible stocks through a single-price call auction, replacing the earlier method of averaging prices from the last 30 minutes of trading. The system, similar to mechanisms used in China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and South Korea, was designed to prevent market participants from artificially influencing closing prices.

Orders during CAS can be placed within a 3% band of a reference price calculated from the volume-weighted average between 3:00 p.m. and 3:15 p.m. IST. But thin liquidity on the BSE, where Sensex contracts trade, has consistently amplified price swings during the auction window.

Traders Call for Pause

"Put sellers will be at loss today due to these sharp moves. We have advised clients to close trades before closing auction begins as it is very difficult to predict what would happen in those fifteen to twenty minutes."

— Ratnesh Goyal, Head Technical and Derivatives Analyst, Arihant Capital Markets

Rajesh Palviya, senior vice president and head of research at Axis Securities, said the volatility is drawing speculative traders seeking "jackpot profits" while pushing regular participants to cut positions ahead of the auction. Motilal Oswal's derivatives head Chandan Taparia said the firm now advises clients to reduce option writing near expiry and shift toward long strangles.

Last week, former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya urged SEBI to temporarily suspend and redesign CAS following a similar 2,200-point Sensex swing on August 27. Rohit Srivastava, founder of Indiacharts.com, said the problem is pace of implementation — most retail trading platforms are not yet equipped for the auction's specific order types.

Broader Market Impact

The disruption is already affecting broader market participation. Average daily turnover on the NSE fell 3% in August to Rs 1,16,579 crore from Rs 1,20,416 crore in July, hitting a five-month low, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. Persistent stake sales by promoters and a strong IPO pipeline have also dampened secondary market appetite.

Meanwhile, the CAS has created unusual trading patterns around the 3:15 p.m. cutoff. On Tuesday, heavyweight Reliance Industries extended gains from 2% to 2.5% ahead of CAS, while ICICI Bank pared losses from 1.8% to 1.1% — suggesting large players are repositioning ahead of the auction window.

What to Watch

SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has said the regulator would take strict action against manipulation attempts but has not indicated plans to modify the CAS framework. With Sensex weekly expiries now triggering multi-thousand-point swings regularly, the pressure on SEBI to either improve liquidity participation or pause the rollout is mounting ahead of the next expiry cycle.
